title: Was It on the Bus or at the Station?
prerequisites: Recognise common transport and bag words
understand a simple past event with left
observable_outcome: The learner distinguishes the transport from the station, states the exact position, and gives two identifying features.
learning_objective: Clarify whether a lost item was left on a bus or at the station, then describe it for identification.

scenario.setting: A phone call to a lost-property desk.
scenario.prompt: Your small black backpack is missing. You remember putting it under a seat near the back of the number 12 bus. It has a red zip tag and a front pocket.
scenario.puzzle: Was it left on the bus or at the station, and which details can help staff identify it?
scenario.privacy_note: The lost-property desk, route, person, and bag are fictional teaching data.

model.clarify: I think I left it on the number 12 bus, not at the station.
model.customer_reply: It's a small black backpack with a red zip tag and a front pocket.
model.confirm: So that's bus 12, under a seat near the back, correct?
model.neutral_variant: I believe it was on bus 12. It's small and black, with a red zip tag.

language_focus.grammar: Use on with public transport such as a bus or train, and at with a place used as a point, such as a station. With can add identifying features: a backpack with a red zip tag.
language_focus.meaning: The route and exact position tell staff where to search. Size, colour, item type, and distinctive features help distinguish one bag from another.
language_focus.appropriateness: I think or I believe honestly shows that a memory may be uncertain. Not at the station corrects the alternative. A short confirmation lets both people check the location before ending the call.
language_focus.detail_language: Small black backpack is a natural compact description here. The lesson models size before colour before the item, but it does not claim that every English adjective sequence follows one universal rule.

choice_activity.prompt: Which location best matches the memory?

options.feedback: Correct. You remember putting the bag under a seat near the back of bus 12.
The station is the alternative, but the evidence points to a seat on bus 12.
No taxi appears in the memory. Use the route and seat clue: on bus 12.

request_activity.prompt: Which description gives useful identifying evidence?

options.text: It's a small black backpack with a red zip tag and a front pocket.
options.feedback: Correct. It gives item type, size, colour, and two visible features.

options.text: It's a bag. I really need it.
options.feedback: The need is understandable, but 'a bag' is too general. Add colour, size, and a distinctive feature.
Nice and new are subjective or hard to verify. Give visible details such as colour, tag, and pocket.

slot_activity.prompt: Match each clue to its information slot.

feedback.transport: Correct. The route identifies the vehicle to search.
feedback.exact position: Under a seat near the back is the exact position.
feedback.identifying feature: The red zip tag and front pocket identify the bag itself.

items.detail: under a seat near the back

feedback.transport: The transport is the number 12 bus.
feedback.exact position: Correct. This narrows the search to one part of the bus.
feedback.identifying feature: This describes where the bag was, not what the bag looks like.

items.detail: red zip tag and front pocket

feedback.transport: The transport clue is number 12 bus.
feedback.exact position: The position is under a seat near the back.
feedback.identifying feature: Correct. These visible features can distinguish the backpack from similar black bags.

production_task.scenario: You left an umbrella on train 6, on the overhead rack. It has a blue curved handle and a name label.
production_task.instruction: Write one location clarification, one identifying description, and one confirmation question.
acceptable_responses: I think I left it on train 6, not at the station. It was on the overhead rack. It's a black umbrella with a blue curved handle and a name label. So that's train 6, on the overhead rack, correct?
I believe it was on train 6. It's an umbrella with a blue curved handle and a name label. That's train 6 and the overhead rack, right?
rubric: I distinguished the vehicle from the station.
I named the route and exact position.
I gave the item type and visible features.
I ended with a confirmation question.
production_task.valid_variants: I think and I believe can both mark uncertain memory. On train 6 and aboard train 6 can work. Right?, correct?, and Is that right? can all invite confirmation.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, recall the three lost-item slots: transport, exact position, and identifying features. Describe one imaginary item using all three.

visual.title: Place, position, features
visual.alt_text: A colourful layered papercut flow. A bus card selects on bus 12 rather than at the station; a backpack moves under a rear seat; a red zip tag and front pocket attach; then transport, exact position, and identifying-feature cards stack beside a check mark.
visual.prose: First choose the vehicle or place from the evidence: on bus 12, not at the station. Next state the exact position: under a seat near the back. Then describe the item with visible identifying features. Finish by reading back the transport and position for confirmation.
